newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks dip, no major changes likely.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks dip, no major changes likely.

text.p: Croatian stocks took another dip on Thursday as trade picked up, and market participants said no major changes were likely in the immediate future.
"This is a period of stabilisation," Nenad Pavletic of Auctor brokerage told Reuters, but he named two banks -- Varazdinska and Dalmatinska -- as likely to break the trend.
Seven of 11 active stocks fell, only two rose, one was flat and one traded for the first time. Turnover doubled to 8.1 million kuna on a slightly smaller volume of 7,150 shares.
Varazdinska Banka (VABA)'s first issue stock was today's biggest gainer, surging 75 percent to 28,000 kuna but only one share was sold.
The bank said on Thursday it expected 1996 net of roughly 28 million kuna, compared to 19 million in 1995.
"VABA is an exceptional stock with good fundamentals. It will definitely rise, the same as Dalmatinska," said Pavletic, but added that the latter's growth might be limited by short supply.
Dalmatinska sold 2,150 shares at 510 kuna on its debut.
Blue chip Pliva pharmaceutical was absent from the market for the first time in months as its Zagreb price overshot the $16.475 its 1/5 GDRs are fetching on the London Stock Exchange.
Traders foresaw a correction of a few percentage points which would then boost trade.
The other fully-listed stock Zagrebacka Banka ordinaries traded lower at 1,740/1,810 kuna, closing at the bottom of the range or 89 kuna down.
"Blue chips are losing breath and investors are on the look out for new companies," said Pavletic.
Food concern Podravka was the most actively traded stock, ending nine kuna lower at 305 kuna on volume of 2,375 units.
Four active hoteliers extended their losses but traded volume was slow. Istraturist, which slid five kuna to 205, was the most active with 465 units sold.
